subject: art-design
title: Renaissance & Impressionism
welcome_lead: From Da Vinci's perfection to Monet's shimmer of light.
meta_desc: KS3 art movements: Renaissance and Impressionism key features.
final_note: Art movements answer the question 'what should art look like now?'

concepts.def: Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa.
Illusion of depth on a flat surface.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Renaissance began in Italy around 1400. Artists like Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo studied anatomy, perspective and light to paint convincingly realistic figures.
In 1870s Paris, painters like Monet and Renoir worked outside (en plein air), using quick, visible brushstrokes to capture changing light, not perfect detail.
Renaissance painting hides the brushstrokes — surfaces look smooth and lifelike. Impressionism celebrates strokes — close up it looks messy, but step back and the colours mix in your eye.
